AfterObtained.rationale: Re-verdicted from gap by the 2026-07-26 fix pass: the only reason this hook was a gap was guard G1's candidate-filter finding, and G1 rested on a misread class. CORRECTED by the 2026-07-26 relic fix pass. The previous entry quoted `sts2_rl/enchantments.py:158-164` as 'the sim's Swift predicate' and filed a gap against it. THAT IS THE WRONG CLASS: sts2_rl/enchantments.py:158-164 is `SpiralEnchantment.can_enchant`, whose Basic-Strike/Defend predicate yields exactly ['defend', 'strike']. `SwiftEnchantment` (sts2_rl/enchantments.py:473-493) declares NO `can_enchant` at all and inherits the base `Enchantment.can_enchant` at sts2_rl/enchantments.py:119-129. EXECUTED: Swift can enchant 168 of the 203 ported cards, not 2. The two sources that blocked the original audit are now settled. (1) `src/Core/Models/Enchantments/Swift.cs` declares no `CanEnchant` override, so C# Swift eligibility is exactly `EnchantmentModel.CanEnchant` (src/Core/Models/EnchantmentModel.cs:273-294). (2) BeautifulBracelet.cs:31 calls the prefs overload of `CardSelectCmd.FromDeckForEnchantment` that forwards `additionalFilter: null`, so the filter at CardSelectCmd.cs:549 is `Where(c => enchantment.CanEnchant(c) && true)` -- no extra clause. The sim's base `can_enchant` mirrors EnchantmentModel.CanEnchant clause for clause. audit/records/relic/electric_shrymp.json guard N1 had already published this answer at the sibling enchant relic and nobody reconciled this record (binding rule 3). CLAUSE BY CLAUSE at this site: C# rejects CardType Status/Curse/Quest (EnchantmentModel.cs:275-279, the decompiled `(uint)(type - 4) <= 2u`), the sim rejects CardType.STATUS/CURSE/QUEST (sts2_rl/enchantments.py:125-126); C# rejects a card whose `CanEnchantCardType` says no (EnchantmentModel.cs:280-283) and Swift.cs overrides neither `CanEnchant` nor `CanEnchantCardType`, so the default `return true` (EnchantmentModel.cs:258-261) applies and there is nothing for the sim to mirror; C# rejects an Unplayable card sitting in the DECK pile (EnchantmentModel.cs:284-288) and the sim rejects `not card.is_playable` (sts2_rl/enchantments.py:127-128) -- broader in principle, identical here because Beautiful Bracelet only ever looks at `run.deck`; and C# rejects an already-enchanted card unless `IsStackable` (EnchantmentModel.cs:289-292), which is false by default (EnchantmentModel.cs:173) and unoverridden by Swift, matching the sim's `return card.enchantment is None` (sts2_rl/enchantments.py:129). Rule 7: sts2_rl/enchantments.py, src/Core/Models/EnchantmentModel.cs, src/Core/Models/Enchantments/Swift.cs and src/Core/Commands/CardSelectCmd.cs are cited here and not all hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: the enchant AMOUNT is passed twice in C# -- once to the selector prefs for display and once to CardCmd.Enchant<Swift>(item, 3m) (BeautifulBracelet.cs:31, 33) -- and the second call hard-codes 3m rather than reading the DynamicVar
guards.rationale: The literal 3m and DynamicVars['Swift'] (3m) agree, so the source's inconsistency is harmless; the sim uses one constant SWIFT_AMOUNT = 3 for both. Recorded because a future ascension or balance change to the DynamicVar would desync C# itself, and an auditor re-reading this file should not mistake the sim's single constant for the bug.

guards.what: N2: NCardEnchantVfx.Create + the CardPreviewContainer append (BeautifulBracelet.cs:34-38) and the ExtraHoverTips
guards.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status = RelicStatus.* are presentation only (the relic card's glow and its greyed/active state in the relic bar); the sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

guards.what: N3: HasUponPickupEffect is NOT overridden by BeautifulBracelet.cs, and the sim leaves the default False
guards.rationale: Checked for the same reason as relic/arcane_scroll's N4: the flag drives Relic.is_tradable and three relics in this batch do override it. BeautifulBracelet.cs declares Rarity, CanonicalVars, ExtraHoverTips and AfterObtained only.
